title: Hacker House Medellín reservations API
description: The JSON API implemented by hhm-api-server.rs and by its twin crate hhm-api (both register the same four routes over the same types). Keys are operations; values are typed routes. Every parameter and payload names a type in `types`, so the generated clients type-check against this file.

ReservationId.doc: Server-minted id for one reservation. Distinct from a bare string so a client cannot pass an arbitrary id.

ReservationStatus.doc: RESERVATION_STATUSES in main.rs. The handler trims and lowercases the incoming string before checking it against this set, so these are exactly the values that survive validation and the only ones a stored record can carry.

Reservation.doc: One stay, as the API stores and returns it. Field order follows the Rust struct.

CreateReservation.doc: Request body for creating a stay. Every field is required: the Rust struct carries no `#[serde(default)]` and no `Option<..>`, so a missing key fails in the `Json<..>` extractor before the handler runs. `notes` is required but may be the empty string.

member_name.doc: Trimmed; must be non-empty and at most 200 characters.

room_type.doc: Trimmed; must be non-empty and at most 100 characters.

check_out.doc: Must be strictly after `check_in`, and no more than 366 days later.

workspace_plan.doc: Trimmed; must be non-empty and at most 100 characters.

notes.doc: Trimmed; at most 4000 characters. May be empty.

ReservationEvent.doc: The frame broadcast on the websocket after a create. It is not an HTTP response body, so no route declares it; it is declared here because it is part of the wire contract.

event.doc: Always `reservation.created` today -- the only event the server emits.

ApiError.doc: The error envelope every failing handler returns.

healthz.summary: Liveness plus which optional backends are configured.

create_reservation.summary: Create a stay. Responds 201 with the stored record.
create_reservation.doc: Queued through opto-sync: this is the org's one durable write, and hhm-sync is built to reconcile exactly these records (it merges arrays by `id` with last-writer-wins on `updated_at`). The queue mints its own record id because the request body carries none -- the server mints the authoritative `Reservation.id` when it accepts the call.

reservation_events.summary: Websocket upgrade. Frames are `ReservationEvent` JSON; the server answers ping with pong and sends nothing else.
